findings.title: AI admin pagination uses stale React state and does not page correctly
findings.description: AISupervisionAdmin.load() closes over the current cursor, useEffect only runs on mount, and next/previous handlers call setTimeout(load, 0) immediately after setCursor(). The fetch therefore reuses stale state instead of the requested page, and previousPage always resets to cursor 0 rather than the actual previous cursor.
findings.snippet: adminApi.aiRequests(cursor)...; useEffect(() => { load() }, []); const nextPage = () => { if (nextCursor > 0) { setCursor(nextCursor); setTimeout(load, 0) } }
findings.recommendation: Make cursor the single source of truth as the other admin pagers already do: either call load(nextCursor) with an explicit argument and keep cursor history, or fetch from useEffect([cursor]) instead of relying on a stale closure.
findings.impact: Admins cannot reliably inspect older AI request records, so the new AI governance panel misreports history and weakens manual review of auto-adopt behavior.

findings.title: AI advisory validation is not EOF-strict after the first JSON object
findings.description: ValidateAdvisory() uses json.Decoder with DisallowUnknownFields, but it only performs one Decode call and never verifies that the decoder reached EOF. A provider response that contains one valid advisory followed by extra prose or a second JSON object will still be accepted.
findings.snippet: dec := json.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(trimmed)); dec.DisallowUnknownFields(); if err := dec.Decode(&adv); err != nil { ... }
findings.recommendation: Require EOF after the first decode and add a regression test for fenced JSON with trailing text or concatenated objects so the AI gate remains strictly fail-closed.
findings.impact: This weakens the promised JSON-only trust boundary for the optional AI subsystem: malformed provider output can enter advisory or auto-adopt evaluation instead of being rejected deterministically.

findings.title: Live-check verification script hardcodes an absolute repository path
findings.description: run-live-check.bat changes into E:\Sillytarvennew\stcontrol explicitly, while the paired run-live-controller.bat correctly uses %~dp0. In this reviewed worktree the repository lives under E:\dshtest\Sillytarvennew\stcontrol, so the live-check script starts from the wrong directory before touching pg_ctl/psql.
findings.recommendation: Use cd /d %~dp0 and keep the rest of the script relative, matching run-live-controller.bat, so local verification works from any clone or flash worktree path.
findings.impact: The intended live-check gate is non-portable and already broken in the current flash worktree, which can block or mislead operators during controller verification.

cross_references.reason: Broken pagination also blocks the admin-side verification workflow for AI requests.
Validator strictness is part of the trust boundary for AI-generated input.
The scripted verification path is part of the release/test gate and is currently non-portable.
